text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("In Endless Dark: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} Culture"). These are informal outlooks, not organizations with membership rolls — a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} character can be built around one as a philosophy and social orientation within the clan and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}.

The Factionless: Most Lasombra identify themselves this way — "I'm a Lasombra and a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}" — without worrying about finer subgroup distinctions or feeling driven to align with any of the outlooks below.

The Crusaders: A minority who view the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} as a religious and military organization almost to the exclusion of the Sabbat as an ideology of personal freedom. More elders favor this approach than neonates. Sect-wide, the Ultra-Conservative faction includes Lasombra and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} elders alongside some antitribu elders, especially @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}.

The Faithful: In earlier nights many Lasombra took Christianity (and smaller numbers Judaism, Islam, and other faiths) very seriously, regarding themselves as servitors of God locked into certain or near-certain damnation. The late Cardinal Monçada personified this approach and survived the destruction of many former comrades; with his passing, the Faithful lack a strong leader. Half a dozen rivals — almost all Latin American or Mediterranean archbishops — vie to be recognized as "Monçada's heir," with Archbishop Menard of Nicaragua currently holding the most widespread support.

The Black Angels (Angellis Ater): Since the first Christian centuries, some Lasombra have interpreted their role as literal devils on earth, serving Satan's will by feeding both moral and physical darkness. In the Middle Ages the Black Angels constantly provoked the Friends of the Night with reckless, relentless assaults on mortal society; in the last thirty years or so they have re-emerged from the margins of Lasombra culture.

The Abyss's Children: Dedicated practitioners of Abyss mysticism, who care about the Sabbat mainly as a safe space in which to pursue their studies. No single city hosts more than a handful of the Children, but secret enclaves of Abyss mystics reputedly exist far from known Sabbat strongholds.

The Kings and Queens of Shadow: Lasombra who take the vampiric condition as a mandate to rule directly over humanity, performing much of the function ghouls serve within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}. Despite the grandiose name, they are nearly outcasts within their own clan, and they must retain Humanity rather than adopt a Path of Enlightenment or lose most of their ability to mingle with mortals at all.

The Corsairs: Lasombra who take a full-time interest in the sea, running private shipping empires and feeding on crews and passengers while moving their havens from vessel to vessel. A handful deal in the world's navies outright — at least one fast attack submarine, a Soviet Kilo-class boat sold to Iran in 1995 and reported "lost at sea" two years later, is in Lasombra hands; the Black Fang preys primarily on @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}-controlled shipping. (Storyteller note: such arrangements are plausible via a vampire with connections to a maritime engineering firm who can arrange for a Navy or scientific submarine to be "lost" amid inter-agency record-keeping errors.)

The Transhumanists: Since before recorded history, some Lasombra have made mastery of their full implicit potential their primary goal, quantifying their powers, working out taxonomies, and otherwise seeking to reduce vampirism itself to data.

The Fatalists: Fatalists do not admit to the label if they wish to avoid destruction. Their single doctrine: that no matter how things appear, they possess no actual free will.

The Doomed: Lasombra who style themselves heroes, warriors, or other self-congratulatory titles, aiming at the immediate conquest of everything in sight. Most other Lasombra destroy such clanmates on sight.

pages.name: The Lasombra Antitribu: Reactionaries and Radicals

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("The Unkept: The Antitribu").

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} antitribu never call themselves antitribu. Lineages that reject the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} do so for one of two diametrically opposed reasons:

Reactionaries: The majority of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}-rejecting @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, who remain attached to the traditional (if outdated) order of clan hierarchy and childe-sire relations. Most support the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, though roughly a third of the conservative lineages steer an altogether independent course. Reactionary antitribu usually value Humanity, and when they adopt a Path of Enlightenment at all, favor scholarly, sedate ones.

The Distinguished: A subfaction within the reactionary Keepers who prosecute their war against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} through espionage and sabotage rather than direct confrontation, and who maintain the antitribu's famous pirate fleets.

Radicals: Their complaint about the Sabbat is that it doesn't go far enough. Radicals fully accept that vampires are innately inhuman, and venerate the Antediluvian as darkness incarnate. They practice Obtenebration and, whenever they can find instructors, Thaumaturgy, with consummate devotion, and seldom retain Humanity for very long.

Becoming antitribu: The antitribu choose their childer much as Sabbat Lasombra do, including testing to destruction or near-destruction — some push this further still, since so few antitribu exist that the lineage cannot afford even one deadbeat or marginal childe. The reactionaries have experimented on at least three occasions with mass Embrace in the style of Sabbat "shovel parties"; all three attempts ended in the slaughter of the new childer.

pages.name: Defecting from the Sabbat: Vinculum Thresholds

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("Defection from the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}").

Successfully leaving the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} to join the antitribu takes time, and the Vinculum itself is the chief obstacle. A vampire with extensive Vinculum bonds probably cannot manage it at all:

  • Vinculum rating 3 or higher: the knowledge that she is joining the enemy is sufficient to make unlife actively uncomfortable — defection is possible but psychologically painful.
  • Vinculum rating 6 or higher: defection becomes difficult; the bonded loyalty actively fights the attempt.
  • Vinculum rating 7 or higher: defection is almost altogether impossible.

Even among those who make the attempt, perhaps only one defector in ten actually ends up finding and being accepted by the antitribu clanmates she hoped to join, and it takes years or decades of proving herself to fully earn trust and standing among them.

MET/Storyteller note: Storytellers running a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} defection plot should treat the character's current Vinculum rating(s) as a hard mechanical gate on the attempt, using the thresholds above (3/6/7+) to scale the difficulty of any related Willpower or Discipline-resistance tests, and should expect the roleplaying payoff (if the attempt even succeeds) to unfold over an extended, multi-session arc of earning antitribu trust rather than a single scene.

pages.name: Lasombra Relations: Clan, Sect, and Beyond

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("The Clan and the World"), condensing in-character elder commentary on other clans, sects, and supernatural creatures.

Standing in the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} make up roughly a quarter of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s total membership, but fill more than a third of its offices, and in some cities hold an actual majority of titled leadership positions. Elder @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} tend to feel deeply possessive of the sect they helped found.

Among themselves: Lasombra pride themselves on doing everything with style and elegance. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} Lasombra vigorously deny keeping anything like the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} customs of Elysium and salon — though in practice most Lasombra gather and trade news and views with like-minded associates in settings policed against random violence, which amounts to much the same thing.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}: The clan's closest allies and most bitter competitors within the Sabbat. Lasombra never let the Fiends forget that the Lasombra initiated the revolt that produced the Sabbat — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} simply resent coming in second on anything.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers}: regarded as cannon fodder, an experiment that has not yet earned respect.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls}: disturbing; best handled by trusted subordinates rather than directly.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.gB6sZrC1J50lqpub]{Kiasyd}: mysterious; a standing reward is offered within the clan to any student who learns more about them.

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.RXFNMUlZX4WmZVOj]{Panders}: more cannon fodder, useful chiefly for interfering with @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} plans.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} (general): described as a mob putting its finest vitae into captivity to serve manipulators who ultimately want to consume them all. Per-clan opinions (voiced in-character):

  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}: "the parasites' parasites" — pathetic, prideful about a rebellion it cannot actually execute.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}: wasted potential — could rule the wilds as gods of chaos if they had vision and organization; worth occasional recruitment.
  • Malkavians: visionary or lunatic; their blood curse's true nature is unclear, possibly a botched imitation of the Lasombra's own relationship to the Abyss.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}: shifty and clever, and see too much even through Lasombra darkness; kept busy investigating rivals to keep them occupied.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}: poetry and beauty used as bait; a shadow-transformed Lasombra using Black Metamorphosis can captivate @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} admirers.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}: one of the few @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} clans taken seriously, given their systematic study of Thaumaturgy.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}: "Think of the Lasombra. Subtract the intelligence, the forethought, the style and the dedication to supremacy. That's the Blue Bloods: like us, but stupid."

The Independents:

  • Assamites: harder to track since the breaking of their curse; the Black Hand's disarray is treated as opportunity, but the clan urges caution.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set}: useful business associates within careful boundaries — though too many Lasombra condemned before the Courts of Blood believed "one more deal couldn't hurt."
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}: largely uninteresting, though their necromantic obsessions may approach the Abyss from a different angle.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}: hated; the wisest course is to retreat into shadow and wait for a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} to leave an area, since they weaken all undead social structures they pass through.
  • Cathayans (the Pentuple/Crossed Court): the Asian vampire sect, comprising at least three (perhaps up to eight) distinct clans; their territorial expansion around the Pacific Rim bears watching.

Other creatures:

  • Lupines: stay out of their way; exploit the urban advantage against them, and feed them sacrifices or simply relocate rather than contest their territory.
  • Magicians: too dangerous to study closely; steer clear except when they directly threaten current activities.
  • Ghosts: avoid as a rule, though occasionally profitable to deal with if any bargain is kept clear and strictly bounded.
  • Changelings: not considered worth pursuing.
  • Hunters: never assume total understanding of kine society; nothing about modern witch-hunters seems fundamentally new, but the clan counsels staying alert regardless.

pages.name: Clan Life: Rhythms, Havens, and Shadow Occultism

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two (assorted sidebars).

The Death of Ambition: A vampire unable to cope with the limitations of undeath is very likely to develop derangements or simply lose all self-control and perish in a final fury of Wassail. The suicidal behavior of such neonates ranks among the major causes of Final Death within the clan.

The Rhythms of the Night: Only the rare @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} with extremely high Fortitude can routinely resist the pull of daysleep, and low Humanity forces a vampire to sleep longer after sunset. Averaged over a year, the highest-Humanity vampires get roughly 12 waking hours per night; nearly all @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} vampires, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} included, get substantially less — as little as eight or nine hours. At least an hour nightly typically goes to feeding, with the rites, auctoritas, and ignoblis of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} life consuming still more, leaving most Lasombra only a few free hours a night for their own pursuits.

I See You (haven mirrors): Lasombra havens, whatever else distinguishes them, almost always fall to one of two extremes regarding mirrors: either mirrored on virtually every surface, or containing no mirrors or reflective surfaces of any kind.

Shadow Occultism (Ability variant): Many Lasombra lineages teach a stripped-down version of the Occult Ability called Shadow Occultism. A vampire who learns this restricted body of technique gains only fragmentary insight into the wider realm of occult study — when using Shadow Occultism for any purpose other than supporting Obtenebration, halve the Ability rating, rounding down. Lasombra characters may instead learn full Occult with an Abyss specialty by studying the clan's accumulated lore on the subject; non-Lasombra learn Abyss mysticism only rarely, either as a reward for exceptional service (with a strict non-teaching stipulation) or, in earlier ages, by studying abandoned occult libraries. The Abyss specialty applies to Obtenebration use and to the knowledge or performance of rites tied to gods of darkness, death, and destruction; at Storyteller discretion, Lasombra thaumaturges gain the same bonus toward darkness- and destruction-themed blood magic.
